findings.title: Check output drops skipped merge commits
findings.description: The `check` branch in `src/cli.ts` builds stdout from failing commits, malformed records, and the summary without printing `skip <short sha> merge commit` for skipped merges. When the input contains merge commits, maintainers and CI see only the skipped count, and the all-merge test still passes because it checks only the exit code and summary.

findings.title: Some control characters in commit headers still reach the terminal raw
findings.description: The `check` branch prints failing headers with `JSON.stringify(c.header)` and interpolates malformed-record reasons without applying `oneLine()`, leaving DEL, C1 controls, Unicode line separators, and bidi or other invisible formatting characters unescaped. A crafted commit header or malformed stream record, including an invalid-SHA reason, can use those characters to reorder or spoof a `fail` line or make it appear to break across lines on terminals that interpret them.

findings.title: Malformed-record lines can carry unescaped control characters
findings.description: `malformed ${m.reason}` prints the parser's reason with nothing applied, and for a bad SHA that reason is `invalid sha: ${JSON.stringify(sha)}` built from the raw stream bytes (src/gitlog.ts:71). C1 controls, NEL, U+2028/U+2029 and bidi marks in a corrupted or crafted record therefore reach check's stdout raw and can split or spoof the line that CI or a maintainer reads.

review_agent_comment:
Before relying on the checker’s output in terminal or CI logs, please harden its escaping: commit messages are untrusted input.

Could you also update linked issue #27 to match the revised criterion 4? It still describes `<header>` as the text Git supplied, while the criterion now uses the parsed `raw` first line, with trailing whitespace and CRs removed.

Please have the merge-only test assert exact stdout, not just the exit code, so the output order is covered.
